name: Graveline Pictures
description: A mid-tier independent studio operating out of a converted water reclamation facility in the Tier 2 fringe, Graveline Pictures specializes in gritty neural-feed crime dramas and labor-conflict thrillers that draw heavily from actual the Gray Zone casework and union testimony. Founded by former Vantablack script editor Caoimhe Nzinga-Hartwell after she was blacklisted for leaking internal content suppression memos, the studio maintains technical licensing through a shell arrangement that Vantablack's legal division has been attempting to unwind for seven years. Their productions are known for an unusually tactile immersion quality — viewers consistently report that Graveline feeds feel more physically present and less aesthetically polished than corporate output, a quality the studio markets as 'honest weight.'
cultural_impact: Graveline's 2201 production 'The Debt Floor' is credited with introducing the term 'honest weight' into GLMZ critical vocabulary, a phrase now used broadly to distinguish immersive content that prioritizes physical realism over emotional manipulation.
story_hooks: A Graveline researcher embedded in the Gray Zone communities to gather testimony for an upcoming production discovers that one of her interview subjects is actively wanted by a corponation security division — and that the studio's shell licensing arrangement may have quietly sold access to their raw feed archives.

Caoimhe Nzinga-Hartwell approaches a fixer with a job: retrieve a stolen production drive from a former Graveline editor who left to work for Vantablack and took three years of unreleased testimony footage with them.

A Tier 3 distributor offers Graveline a legitimate co-production deal that would fund their next three projects — but the contract contains a clause granting content approval rights to an unnamed third-party corponation affiliate buried six layers deep in the subsidiary structure.
